analyst_view.overall: CSKA Sofia (28th, 1 pt) host Trabzonspor (12th, 6 pts) in the first European game at their renovated stadium and need points to stay in the top-24 race. CSKA, under Markus Gisdol, lead the Bulgarian league but drew 3-3 at Botev Plovdiv at the weekend after coming back from 2-0 down; Gisdol called Trabzonspor a very strong side. Trabzonspor beat Eyupspor 1-0 on Sunday, and Thomas Reis said none of his injured players will be back for Sofia, so his European squad will look different: Dju (their top European scorer), Malinovskyi and Batagov are out on top of Simsir and Yokuslu, whom the numbers already count; Folcarelli is back in training but reports differ on whether he plays. Trabzonspor also face Goztepe and Fenerbahce soon after, and no referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.6 of them Trabzonspor's, and they only take off Simsir and Yokuslu. I lean a little lower: Reis confirmed none of the injured return, so Trabzonspor travel without Dju, their top European scorer, and playmaker Malinovskyi, which the numbers can't see; CSKA's 3-3 at Botev keeps it from going further. A mild -4% gives about 2.6 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, split evenly. CSKA must attack at home and Trabzonspor like to push their full-backs, but the numbers already add a little for both sides' recent corner counts, and the absences don't change how either side plays wide, so I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, slightly above a usual game and already nudged up for both sides' recent cards. A must-win home game in a newly reopened, loud stadium can get heated, but nothing specific such as a named referee or a feud points further, so I stay at about 5.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.8 shots, already lifted 12% for CSKA's recent volume. CSKA chasing their first European win should keep the game open, while a weakened Trabzonspor may shoot less; those roughly cancel, so I stay at about 29.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, already raised for CSKA's recent accuracy. Without Dju and Malinovskyi, Trabzonspor lose much of their finishing and chance creation, which the numbers don't know about, so I lean slightly lower: -3% gives about 10.0.
